foir.why: Industry-cited ideal FOIR range is 40-50%; using the upper bound as a single assumed cap.
foir.source: Poonawalla Fincorp, L&T Finance, IndusInd Bank (mid-2026); our judgement within the cited range

retirementAge.why: Approximate lender-cap convention for loan-end age by income type. Only 'salaried' is wired into the engine so far.

personalLoanRateBands.why: Never default unknown credit score to worst-case or best-case; widest band + low confidence instead.
personalLoanRateBands.source: Finance Buddha, OnePaisa, FinanceFunda, Paisabazaar (mid-2026, personal loan segment)

businessLoanRateBands.why: Unsecured business loan rates run higher than personal loans and vary more by lender type (PSU banks lower, NBFCs/digital lenders higher). Tiered by credit score using the same relative spread logic as the personal-loan table, anchored to the observed overall market range.
businessLoanRateBands.source: DMI Finance, FlexiLoans, Shardaassociates, IIFL (mid-2026); overall observed range roughly 8-26% across lender types, narrowed here to a usable band

lapRateBands.why: Loan Against Property is secured, so rates run well below unsecured business/personal loans. This replaces the earlier unverified 'securedRate' placeholder (9-12%) added in the collateral-logic change.
lapRateBands.source: Poonawalla Fincorp, BankBazaar, HDFC Bank, Central Bank of India (mid-2026); market range converges around 9-14% for good credit profiles

twoWheelerRateBands.why: Electric two-wheeler loans specifically observed at 11-16% p.a. - used as the base band since two of our three personas' loan types are EV/two-wheeler. General (non-electric) two-wheeler loans span a wider 7.6-28% range depending heavily on lender tier; this table reflects the EV-specific, better-sourced figure.
twoWheelerRateBands.source: meraev.com (EV-specific, mid-2026); corroborated by general two-wheeler market data from BankBazaar (Axis, ICICI, SBI, HDFC listings, mid-2026)

processingFee.why: Market-observed range is 0.5-5%; using a mid-range band, not the extremes.

bounceOverride.why: A single old/isolated bounce should not auto-reject; only a RECENT bounce combined with high-cost debt should override the math.

stressCase.why: O4 requires one stress case (income drop or rate rise); chose income drop as the more universally relevant risk across income types.

neededEmiRateStrategy.why: Using the optimistic/low end of the assumed rate band to compute the EMI needed for the requested amount, rather than the midpoint or conservative high end.

selfEmployedConfidence.why: Confidence-only modifier, does not affect core affordability math - a newer business carries more income-continuity uncertainty over the loan's tenure.

collateral.why: Typical LAP lending ceiling as a share of usable (unencumbered) property value.
collateral.source: our judgement, informed by typical LAP industry practice (50-70% LTV range observed)
